Business guide

How to review your business insurance before renewal

Chestnut Insurance Agency editorial team · Published 21 November 2026

Begin at least six to eight weeks before renewal. Update your asset values, confirm that cover still matches how you operate, and decide which covers to retain, change or add, before you compare insurers.

Update the facts

  • New premises, vehicles, equipment or stock levels
  • Changes in headcount and payroll
  • New services, contracts or clients
  • Any claims or incidents since last renewal

Review the values

  • Buildings: rebuilding cost
  • Contents and stock: replacement cost
  • Business interruption: current gross profit and realistic restart time

Check the programme as a whole

  • Look for gaps, such as no liability cover for a new activity
  • Look for overlaps that cost money without adding protection
  • Compare contract insurance requirements with your actual policies

Prepare for the market

  • Gather a clean claims history
  • Describe improvements in security or safety
  • Ask for a comparison of terms, not only premiums

This guide is general education about insurance in Kenya. It is not legal or financial advice and does not describe any specific policy. Policy wording, exclusions and the law that applies at the time govern. Speak to an advisor about your situation.
